spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Sectors, MaxVersion, NoSector

VARIABLES version, folded, outstanding, coordinator, synced

\* A report is a proposed perimeter edit for one sector, stamped with the sector
\* version the observing drone could see when it filed the report.
Reports == [sector : Sectors \cup {NoSector}, stamp : 0..MaxVersion]
Idle == [sector |-> NoSector, stamp |-> 0]

vars == <<version, folded, outstanding, coordinator, synced>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Sectors -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ folded \in [Sectors -> SUBSET (0..MaxVersion)]
    /\ outstanding \in [Drones -> Reports]
    /\ coordinator \in Drones
    /\ synced \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ version = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ folded = [s \in Sectors |-> {}]
    /\ outstanding = [d \in Drones |-> Idle]
    /\ coordinator \in Drones
    /\ synced = TRUE

\* The stamp may lag the map: the drone reports what it could see over the link.
Observe(d, s, v) ==
    /\ outstanding[d] = Idle
    /\ v <= version[s]
    /\ v < MaxVersion
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![d] = [sector |-> s, stamp |-> v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, folded, coordinator, synced>>

\* Reports are folded in whatever order the coordinator draws them, not the
\* order they were filed; a matching stamp is what makes the fold safe.
Fold(d) ==
    /\ synced
    /\ outstanding[d] # Idle
    /\ outstanding[d].stamp = version[outstanding[d].sector]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![outstanding[d].sector] = @ + 1]
    /\ folded' = [folded EXCEPT ![outstanding[d].sector] = @ \cup {outstanding[d].stamp}]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![d] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, synced>>

Discard(d) ==
    /\ synced
    /\ outstanding[d] # Idle
    /\ outstanding[d].stamp # version[outstanding[d].sector]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![d] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, folded, coordinator, synced>>

\* Failover keeps the bag of outstanding reports but costs the new coordinator
\* its knowledge of where each sector stands.
Failover(d) ==
    /\ d # coordinator
    /\ coordinator' = d
    /\ synced' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, folded, outstanding>>

Resync ==
    /\ ~synced
    /\ synced' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, folded, outstanding, coordinator>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors, v \in 0..MaxVersion : Observe(d, s, v)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Fold(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Discard(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Failover(d)
    \/ Resync

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every version step a sector has taken is covered by exactly one folded report:
\* the folded stamps are the gapless run below the sector's current version.
NoLostUpdate == \A s \in Sectors : folded[s] = 0..(version[s] - 1)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {dScout, dRelay, dTanker}
    Sectors = {secNorth, secRidge}
    MaxVersion = 2
    NoSector = noSector

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm maintains one shared perimeter map. The map is
partitioned into sectors, and each sector carries a version number that increases by one
every time an edit is folded in. One drone at a time acts as the swarm's coordinator and
is the only node allowed to fold edits into the map; if it is lost to smoke or battery
failure the swarm elects a replacement.

Any drone may observe a sector and file a perimeter report. The report is stamped with the
sector version the drone could see at the moment of observation, which over a noisy radio
link may already be behind the map. Reports do not arrive in the order they were made:
the coordinator holds a bag of outstanding reports and may fold any one of them in at any
time, so a report filed second can be folded first.

The swarm behaves as follows. A drone with no report outstanding observes some sector and
files a report stamped with any version at or below that sector's current version. The
coordinator, once it has resynchronised, folds an outstanding report into the map when the
report's stamp equals the sector's current version, recording that version step as covered
and advancing the sector's version by one. The coordinator discards an outstanding report
whose stamp does not equal the sector's current version, because folding it would silently
overwrite whatever edit moved the sector forward in the meantime. Any other drone may take
over as coordinator at any time; a fresh coordinator starts unsynchronised and must
resynchronise with the map before it is permitted to fold anything, while the bag of
outstanding reports survives the handover untouched.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every sector, the set of version stamps that have been folded into
the map is exactly the gapless run from zero up to one below that sector's current version,
so every version step the sector has taken is accounted for by exactly one folded report
and none was overwritten unseen.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m9p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Slots, Units, MaxEpoch, Unassigned, Awaiting, NoSlot

VARIABLES epoch, installed, slot, holds, failed

vars == <<epoch, installed, slot, holds, failed>>

\* A slot is either untouched, awaiting a unit, or recording the unit bound to it;
\* "holds" is the mirror view, recording for each unit the slot it went to.
SlotState == {Unassigned, Awaiting} \cup Units

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ installed \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ slot \in [Slots -> SlotState]
    /\ holds \in [Units -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ failed \in SUBSET Nodes

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ installed = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ slot = [s \in Slots |-> Unassigned]
    /\ holds = [u \in Units |-> NoSlot]
    /\ failed = {}

\* Only the node installed at the bank's current epoch may bind, so a node that
\* was demoted while it was merely slow finds its authority already spent.
Authorised(n) == installed[n] = epoch /\ n \notin failed

Request(s) ==
    /\ slot[s] = Unassigned
    /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![s] = Awaiting]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, installed, holds, failed>>

Bind(n, s, u) ==
    /\ Authorised(n)
    /\ slot[s] = Awaiting
    /\ holds[u] = NoSlot
    /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![s] = u]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![u] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, installed, failed>>

\* Installing a successor costs an epoch and strands the previous holder behind.
Install(n) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ n \notin failed
    /\ installed[n] # epoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ installed' = [installed EXCEPT ![n] = epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, holds, failed>>

Fail(n) ==
    /\ n \notin failed
    /\ Cardinality(failed) < Cardinality(Nodes) - 1
    /\ (installed[n] = epoch => epoch < MaxEpoch)
    /\ failed' = failed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, installed, slot, holds>>

\* A restarted node keeps the epoch it remembers, which may already be stale.
Restart(n) ==
    /\ n \in failed
    /\ failed' = failed \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, installed, slot, holds>>

Binding == \E n \in Nodes, s \in Slots, u \in Units : Bind(n, s, u)
Installing == \E n \in Nodes : Install(n)

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Request(s)
    \/ Binding
    \/ Installing
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Restart(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Binding) /\ WF_vars(Installing)

NoDoubleAllocation == \A u \in Units : holds[u] # NoSlot => slot[holds[u]] = u

EveryAwaitingSlotEventuallyBound ==
    \A s \in Slots : (slot[s] = Awaiting) ~> (slot[s] \in Units)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {trkAlpha, trkBeta, trkGamma}
    Slots = {slotMorning, slotEvening}
    Units = {unitOPos, unitABNeg}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    Unassigned = unassigned
    Awaiting = awaiting
    NoSlot = noSlot

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY EveryAwaitingSlotEventuallyBound
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker binds physical blood units to transfusion slots. The bank
runs on a small set of tracker nodes, but only one node at a time is authorised to bind
units, and that authority is carried by an epoch number: a node may bind only while the
epoch it was installed at is still the bank's current epoch. A tracker node can fail
silently, so the rest of the bank cannot tell a dead node from a slow one; suspicion alone
is enough to install a successor at the next epoch, which means a healthy node can be
demoted while it still believes it holds the authority.

The tracker behaves as follows. A transfusion slot that has never been requested may be
requested, putting it into the awaiting state. The node whose installed epoch equals the
bank's current epoch, and that has not failed, may bind a blood unit that is not already
bound to any slot into an awaiting slot; the slot then records the unit and the unit
records the slot. Any non-failed node whose installed epoch is behind the bank's may
install itself at the next epoch, provided the bank has not exhausted its epoch budget;
this is how a suspected node is replaced, and it leaves the previous holder installed at
a stale epoch. A node may fail silently, except that the node currently holding the
authority may only fail while there is still epoch budget left to replace it, and at least
one node always stays up. A failed node may restart; it comes back with the epoch it
remembers, which by then may be stale.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a blood unit records that it is bound to a slot, that slot
records the very same unit back, so no slot is ever bound a second time behind the first
binding's back.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every slot that reaches the awaiting state is eventually bound to a
blood unit.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, MaxRound, MaxOverrides, NoVote, Idle,
          Collecting, Committed, Aborted

VARIABLES round, phase, accepted, executing, authorised

vars == <<round, phase, accepted, executing, authorised>>

\* accepted[c] is the round of the crane's latest acceptance; executing[c] is the
\* round of the plan the crane is physically lifting under, or Idle.
TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ phase \in {Collecting, Committed, Aborted}
    /\ accepted \in [Cranes -> {NoVote} \cup (0..MaxRound)]
    /\ executing \in [Cranes -> {Idle} \cup (0..MaxRound)]
    /\ authorised \in SUBSET Cranes

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ phase = Collecting
    /\ accepted = [c \in Cranes |-> NoVote]
    /\ executing = [c \in Cranes |-> Idle]
    /\ authorised = {}

\* Clearance is either an acceptance of the round now in force or the supervisor's
\* standing override -- nothing else lets a crane touch a container.
Cleared(c) == accepted[c] = round \/ c \in authorised

Accept(c) ==
    /\ phase = Collecting
    /\ accepted[c] # round
    /\ accepted' = [accepted EXCEPT ![c] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, executing, authorised>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = Collecting
    /\ \A c \in Cranes : accepted[c] = round
    /\ phase' = Committed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, accepted, executing, authorised>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = Collecting
    /\ phase' = Aborted
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, accepted, executing, authorised>>

Recollect ==
    /\ phase = Aborted
    /\ phase' = Collecting
    /\ accepted' = [c \in Cranes |-> NoVote]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, executing, authorised>>

StartLift(c) ==
    /\ phase = Committed
    /\ executing[c] = Idle
    /\ Cleared(c)
    /\ executing' = [executing EXCEPT ![c] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, accepted, authorised>>

FinishLift(c) ==
    /\ executing[c] # Idle
    /\ executing' = [executing EXCEPT ![c] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, accepted, authorised>>

\* The yard only re-plans once the quay is quiet; a crane still swinging a box
\* would otherwise be finishing a lift the new plan never sanctioned.
NextRound ==
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ phase # Collecting
    /\ \A c \in Cranes : executing[c] = Idle
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ phase' = Collecting
    /\ UNCHANGED <<accepted, executing, authorised>>

Authorise(c) ==
    /\ c \notin authorised
    /\ Cardinality(authorised) < MaxOverrides
    /\ authorised' = authorised \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, accepted, executing>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Accept(c)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Recollect
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : StartLift(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : FinishLift(c)
    \/ NextRound
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Authorise(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleOrUnclearedLift ==
    \A c \in Cranes :
        executing[c] # Idle => (executing[c] = round /\ Cleared(c))

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {crnQuayA, crnQuayB, crnLasher}
    MaxRound = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
    NoVote = noVote
    Idle = idle
    Collecting = collecting
    Committed = committed
    Aborted = aborted

INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnclearedLift
nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs each lift plan through a two-phase commit across its
cranes. A plan generation is identified by a round number. In the collect phase the yard
gathers one acceptance per crane for the current round; when every crane has accepted the
current round the plan commits, and cranes may execute lifts under it. If the yard gives
up on a round instead, the plan aborts, and the round can be recollected from scratch with
all previous acceptances thrown away. The yard supervisor holds a privileged override: a
small number of cranes may be flagged as supervisor-authorised, and such a crane may
execute lifts under a committed plan even though it never accepted the round.

The yard behaves as follows. A crane whose recorded acceptance is not for the current round
may accept the current round while the yard is collecting. The yard commits the round once
every crane's recorded acceptance is for the current round. The yard may instead abort the
round while collecting. An aborted round may be recollected, which returns the yard to
collecting and erases every crane's recorded acceptance. An idle crane may start a lift
while the plan is committed and the crane either accepted the current round or carries the
supervisor's authorisation; the crane then records the round it is executing under. A crane
that is executing a lift may finish it and go idle. The yard may advance to the next round
once the round budget allows and every crane is idle, which returns the yard to collecting.
The supervisor may authorise a crane, up to the yard's fixed limit on outstanding
authorisations.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a crane is executing a lift, it is executing under the yard's
current round and it either accepted that round or holds the supervisor's authorisation,
so no crane ever acts on a plan generation it was not cleared for.

---- MODULE W4Od13m2p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Writers, Participants, MaxSales, Quiet, Gathering, Prepared

VARIABLES record, confirmed, snapshot, stage, votes

vars == <<record, confirmed, snapshot, stage, votes>>

\* A machine holds the whole record it read, not just its own field, so a stale
\* write-back would take every other machine's count back with it.
Images == [Writers -> 0..MaxSales]
Blank == [w \in Writers |-> 0]

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in Images
    /\ confirmed \in Images
    /\ snapshot \in [Writers -> Images]
    /\ stage \in [Writers -> {Quiet, Gathering, Prepared}]
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Participants

Init ==
    /\ record = Blank
    /\ confirmed = Blank
    /\ snapshot = [w \in Writers |-> Blank]
    /\ stage = [w \in Writers |-> Quiet]
    /\ votes = {}

\* Vote collection is serialised: one write-back gathers at a time, others wait
\* in the prepared state.
Snap(w) ==
    /\ stage[w] = Quiet
    /\ \A x \in Writers : stage[x] # Gathering
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![w] = record]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = Gathering]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, confirmed>>

Vote(w, p) ==
    /\ stage[w] = Gathering
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, confirmed, snapshot, stage>>

Prepare(w) ==
    /\ stage[w] = Gathering
    /\ votes = Participants
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = Prepared]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, confirmed, snapshot>>

\* Validation against the live record is what stops a stale snapshot from
\* overwriting a posting made while it was being voted on.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ stage[w] = Prepared
    /\ snapshot[w] = record
    /\ record[w] < MaxSales
    /\ record' = [snapshot[w] EXCEPT ![w] = @ + 1]
    /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![w] = @ + 1]
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![w] = Blank]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = Quiet]
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

Reject(w) ==
    /\ stage[w] = Prepared
    /\ (snapshot[w] # record \/ record[w] = MaxSales)
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![w] = Blank]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = Quiet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, confirmed, votes>>

Voting == \E w \in Writers, p \in Participants : Vote(w, p)
Preparing == \E w \in Writers : Prepare(w)
Decide(w) == Commit(w) \/ Reject(w)
Deciding == \E w \in Writers : Decide(w)

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Snap(w)
    \/ Voting
    \/ Preparing
    \/ Deciding

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Voting) /\ WF_vars(Preparing)
        /\ \A w \in Writers : WF_vars(Decide(w))

NoLostPosting == \A w \in Writers : record[w] = confirmed[w]

EveryWriteBackEventuallyDecided ==
    \A w \in Writers : (stage[w] # Quiet) ~> (stage[w] = Quiet)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Writers = {vmLobby, vmDepot}
    Participants = {vmLobby, vmDepot, netHub}
    MaxSales = 2
    Quiet = quiet
    Gathering = gathering
    Prepared = prepared

INVARIANT NoLostPosting
PROPERTY EveryWriteBackEventuallyDecided
nl:
A vending machine network keeps one shared sales record holding a running count for each
vending machine. A machine that wants to post a sale does not edit its own field in place:
it takes a snapshot of the whole record, increments its own count in that snapshot, and
later writes the whole snapshot back. Because a write-back replaces the entire record, a
snapshot that has gone out of date would silently erase whatever another machine posted in
the meantime, so every write-back goes through a two-phase commit across the network's
participants and is validated against the live record before it lands.

The network serialises vote collection: at most one write-back gathers votes at a time,
though several may sit prepared and waiting. Participants can be slow but never fail, so a
vote may be arbitrarily late yet always arrives eventually.

The network behaves as follows. A machine with no write-back outstanding may take a
snapshot of the record and start gathering votes, provided no other machine is currently
gathering. Any participant that has not yet voted on the gathering write-back may cast its
vote. Once every participant has voted, the write-back becomes prepared and the vote
tally is cleared for the next one. A prepared write-back commits when its snapshot still
matches the live record exactly and the posting machine is below its sales ceiling: the
record is replaced by the snapshot with the posting machine's count raised by one, and that
machine's own tally of confirmed postings rises by one as well. A prepared write-back is
rejected instead when its snapshot no longer matches the live record or the posting machine
has reached its ceiling, and it leaves the record untouched.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every machine, the count standing in the shared record equals that
machine's own tally of confirmed postings, so no machine's posting is ever erased by
another machine's write-back.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every write-back a machine starts is eventually decided, leaving that
machine with nothing outstanding.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m2p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Locks, NumCreds, MaxPolicy, NoProposal, Shut

VARIABLES newest, proposal, acked, bag, running, standing

vars == <<newest, proposal, acked, bag, running, standing>>

\* Policy p is the point at which credential p joined the household, so a lock
\* running policy p honours credentials 1..p and refuses everything above.
Honours(p) == 1..p

TypeOK ==
    /\ newest \in 0..MaxPolicy
    /\ proposal \in {NoProposal} \cup (1..MaxPolicy)
    /\ acked \in SUBSET Locks
    /\ bag \in [Locks -> SUBSET (1..MaxPolicy)]
    /\ running \in [Locks -> 0..MaxPolicy]
    /\ standing \in [Locks -> {Shut} \cup (1..NumCreds)]

Init ==
    /\ newest = 0
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ bag = [l \in Locks |-> {}]
    /\ running = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ standing = [l \in Locks |-> Shut]

Propose ==
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ newest < MaxPolicy
    /\ proposal' = newest + 1
    /\ acked' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<newest, bag, running, standing>>

Ack(l) ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ l \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<newest, proposal, bag, running, standing>>

CommitPolicy ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ acked = Locks
    /\ newest' = proposal
    /\ bag' = [l \in Locks |-> bag[l] \cup {proposal}]
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ acked' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, standing>>

\* Delivery is unordered, so a lock keeps the later of the arriving policy and the
\* one it is already running rather than trusting arrival order.
Apply(l, p) ==
    /\ p \in bag[l]
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![l] = @ \ {p}]
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![l] = IF p > running[l] THEN p ELSE running[l]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<newest, proposal, acked, standing>>

Admit(l, c) ==
    /\ standing[l] = Shut
    /\ c \in Honours(running[l])
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![l] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<newest, proposal, acked, bag, running>>

Close(l) ==
    /\ standing[l] # Shut
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![l] = Shut]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<newest, proposal, acked, bag, running>>

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Ack(l)
    \/ CommitPolicy
    \/ \E l \in Locks, p \in 1..MaxPolicy : Apply(l, p)
    \/ \E l \in Locks, c \in 1..NumCreds : Admit(l, c)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Close(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnhonouredAdmission ==
    \A l \in Locks : standing[l] # Shut => standing[l] \in Honours(running[l])

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Locks = {lkFront, lkPatio}
    NumCreds = 2
    MaxPolicy = 2
    NoProposal = noProposal
    Shut = shut

INVARIANT NoUnhonouredAdmission
nl:
A smart-home door lock network distributes access policy to its locks. Policies are
numbered, and credentials are numbered too: policy number p is the point at which
credential number p was added to the household, so a lock running policy p honours exactly
credentials one through p and nothing above. A new policy is rolled out by a two-phase
commit across the locks -- the hub proposes the next policy number, every lock
acknowledges it, and only then does the hub commit and broadcast it.

Broadcast is unordered. Each lock accumulates the policy numbers it has been handed in a
delivery bag and applies them one at a time in whatever order they surface, so a lock can
be handed policy two and then policy one. A lock therefore treats an arriving policy as
authoritative only when it is ahead of the one already running; an arrival that is not
ahead is consumed and discarded, because rolling backwards would restore credentials the
household has since moved past.

The network behaves as follows. The hub proposes the next policy number when nothing is
already in flight and the policy budget is not exhausted, clearing the acknowledgement
tally. A lock that has not yet acknowledged the in-flight proposal may acknowledge it. The
hub commits the in-flight proposal once every lock has acknowledged it, recording it as the
newest policy, dropping it into every lock's delivery bag, and clearing the proposal and
the tally. A lock may take any policy number out of its delivery bag and apply it, keeping
whichever of the arriving and the running policy is the later one. A closed lock may admit
a credential that the policy it is running honours, and an open lock may close again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a lock stands open on a credential, that credential is one the
policy the lock is currently running actually honours, so no lock ever admits a credential
on the strength of policy information it should have moved past.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Handlers, Chutes, NoOne, NoChute, Outside, Holding, Working

VARIABLES pier, owner, posture, waiting, notices

vars == <<pier, owner, posture, waiting, notices>>

\* A grant notice names a handler and the chute it reserved; notices are honoured
\* in arbitrary order, so one can outlive the reservation that produced it.
Notices == [who : Handlers, chute : Chutes]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pier \in {NoOne} \cup Handlers
    /\ owner \in [Chutes -> {NoOne} \cup Handlers]
    /\ posture \in [Handlers -> {Outside, Holding, Working}]
    /\ waiting \in [Handlers -> {NoChute} \cup Chutes]
    /\ notices \in SUBSET Notices

Init ==
    /\ pier = NoOne
    /\ owner = [c \in Chutes |-> NoOne]
    /\ posture = [h \in Handlers |-> Outside]
    /\ waiting = [h \in Handlers |-> NoChute]
    /\ notices = {}

TakePier(h) ==
    /\ posture[h] = Outside
    /\ pier = NoOne
    /\ pier' = h
    /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![h] = Holding]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, waiting, notices>>

DropPier(h) ==
    /\ posture[h] = Holding
    /\ waiting[h] = NoChute
    /\ pier' = NoOne
    /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![h] = Outside]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, waiting, notices>>

Reserve(h, c) ==
    /\ posture[h] = Holding
    /\ waiting[h] = NoChute
    /\ owner[c] = NoOne
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = h]
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![h] = c]
    /\ notices' = notices \cup {[who |-> h, chute |-> c]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, posture>>

\* Withdrawing frees the chute but cannot recall the notice already in flight.
Withdraw(h) ==
    /\ posture[h] = Holding
    /\ waiting[h] # NoChute
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![waiting[h]] = NoOne]
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![h] = NoChute]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, posture, notices>>

\* The coarse lock is handed back exactly when the fine lock takes effect.
Honour(n) ==
    /\ n \in notices
    /\ posture[n.who] = Holding
    /\ waiting[n.who] = n.chute
    /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![n.who] = Working]
    /\ pier' = NoOne
    /\ notices' = notices \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, waiting>>

Discard(n) ==
    /\ n \in notices
    /\ (posture[n.who] # Holding \/ waiting[n.who] # n.chute)
    /\ notices' = notices \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, owner, posture, waiting>>

Finish(h) ==
    /\ posture[h] = Working
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![waiting[h]] = NoOne]
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![h] = NoChute]
    /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![h] = Outside]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, notices>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : TakePier(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : DropPier(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, c \in Chutes : Reserve(h, c)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : Withdraw(h)

    \/ \E n \in Notices : Discard(n)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {hdlNorth, hdlSouth}
    Chutes = {chuteA, chuteB}
    NoOne = noOne
    NoChute = noChute
    Outside = outside
    Holding = holding
    Working = working

INVARIANT ChuteExclusion
nl:
An airport baggage router protects its loading chutes with a two-level locking discipline.
A handler must first take the pier lock, which is coarse and held by at most one handler,
and only then reserve one of the fine-grained chute locks. Once the chute is actually in
the handler's hands the pier lock is given back, so the coarse lock is held only for the
short reservation step.

Reservation is not instantaneous: reserving a chute marks the chute as the handler's and
dispatches a grant notice, and notices are processed in whatever order the router gets to
them rather than the order they were dispatched. A handler that grows tired of waiting may
withdraw its reservation, which frees the chute again but leaves the already-dispatched
grant notice in circulation. A grant notice is therefore honoured only when the handler it
names is still holding the pier lock and still waiting for exactly that chute; a notice
that fails this test is a leftover and is thrown away.

The router behaves as follows. A handler that is outside the discipline may take the pier
lock when it is free. A handler holding the pier lock and not yet waiting on a chute may
reserve a free chute, which records the handler as that chute's owner and dispatches a
grant notice. A handler holding the pier lock may withdraw a reservation it is waiting on,
releasing the chute and leaving the notice stale. A handler holding the pier lock and
waiting on no chute may give the pier lock back and step outside. A circulating grant
notice may be honoured when its handler still holds the pier lock and is still waiting for
that exact chute, which puts the handler to work in the chute and returns the pier lock. A
circulating grant notice that fails that test is discarded. A handler at work in a chute
may finish, releasing the chute and stepping outside.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every handler at work in a chute is the handler that chute records as its
owner, so two handlers can never be at work in the same chute at once.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Feeders, MaxTag, NoTag

VARIABLES reg, tag, seen, seenTag, confirmed

vars == <<reg, tag, seen, seenTag, confirmed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in SUBSET Feeders
    /\ tag \in 0..MaxTag
    /\ seen \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Feeders]
    /\ seenTag \in [Controllers -> {NoTag} \cup (0..MaxTag)]
    /\ confirmed \in SUBSET Feeders

Init ==
    /\ reg = {}
    /\ tag = 0
    /\ seen = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ seenTag = [c \in Controllers |-> NoTag]
    /\ confirmed = {}

\* The control bus carries one outstanding read at a time.
Read(c) ==
    /\ \A x \in Controllers : seenTag[x] = NoTag
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![c] = tag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tag, confirmed>>

\* The swap puts back the whole set that was read, so the tag check is what keeps
\* it from erasing anything shed since.
Swap(c, f) ==
    /\ seenTag[c] = tag
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ f \notin seen[c]
    /\ reg' = seen[c] \cup {f}
    /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {f}
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![c] = NoTag]

Undo(c, f) ==
    /\ seenTag[c] = tag
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ f \in seen[c]
    /\ reg' = seen[c] \ {f}
    /\ confirmed' = confirmed \ {f}
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![c] = NoTag]

Abandon(c) ==
    /\ seenTag[c] # NoTag
    /\ seenTag[c] # tag
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![c] = NoTag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tag, confirmed>>

\* The operator's override writes without reading, which is exactly what strands
\* an outstanding read on a tag that has moved.
Force(f) ==
    /\ f \notin reg
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ reg' = reg \cup {f}
    /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {f}
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, seenTag>>

\* Recycling the tag space throws away every outstanding read, so no read can be
\* carried across the reseal and mistaken for a current one.
Reseal ==
    /\ tag = MaxTag
    /\ tag' = 0
    /\ seen' = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ seenTag' = [c \in Controllers |-> NoTag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, confirmed>>

Settling ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, f \in Feeders : Swap(c, f) \/ Undo(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Abandon(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c)
    \/ Settling
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Force(f)
    \/ Reseal

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling) /\ WF_vars(Reseal)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctlEast, ctlWest}
    Feeders = {fdrMill, fdrHarbour}
    MaxTag = 2
    NoTag = noTag

INVARIANT ConfirmedShedsHold
PROPERTY EveryReadEventuallyResolves
nl:
A power-grid load shedder keeps the set of currently shed feeders in a single shared
register guarded by a compare-and-swap tag. A controller that wants to change the set does
not edit it in place: it reads the whole set together with the register's tag, and later
swaps a whole new set back in, but only if the tag it read is still the register's tag.
Because the swap replaces the entire set, a swap made against a tag that has moved on would
silently drop whatever else has been shed in the meantime, so the tag check is the only
thing standing between the grid and a lost shed. The control bus carries one read at a
time, so a controller may only take a fresh read when no read is outstanding.

The grid operator holds a privileged override that bypasses the register discipline
entirely: the operator can force a feeder to be shed immediately, without reading first,
and doing so moves the tag on. That is what puts an outstanding read out of date.

The shedder behaves as follows. A controller may take a read of the register when no read
is outstanding anywhere, recording both the set it saw and the tag it saw. A controller
whose recorded tag still matches the register's tag may swap in the set it read with one
extra feeder shed, moving the tag on and confirming that shed; it may equally swap in the
set it read with one feeder restored, moving the tag on and withdrawing that confirmation.
A controller whose recorded tag no longer matches the register's tag abandons the read and
must start over. The operator may force any feeder to be shed, moving the tag on and
confirming that shed. When the tag space is exhausted the register is resealed: the tag
returns to zero and every outstanding read is thrown away, so no stale read can ever be
mistaken for a current one across the reseal.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every feeder whose shed has been confirmed is still shed in the register,
so no confirmed shed is ever silently dropped by a swap.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every read a controller takes is eventually resolved, leaving that
controller with no read outstanding.

---- MODULE W4Od9m2p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Substations, Participants, MaxEpoch, NoOne

VARIABLES ballot, epoch, tally, holder, posted, atBreaker

vars == <<ballot, epoch, tally, holder, posted, atBreaker>>

\* A grant notice names a substation and the interlock epoch it was posted under;
\* the stamp is all that separates a live grant from a bygone one.
Notices == [to : Substations, stamp : 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ ballot \in {NoOne} \cup Substations
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ tally \in SUBSET Participants
    /\ holder \in {NoOne} \cup Substations
    /\ posted \in SUBSET Notices
    /\ atBreaker \in SUBSET Substations

Init ==
    /\ ballot = NoOne
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ posted = {}
    /\ atBreaker = {}

OpenBallot(s) ==
    /\ ballot = NoOne
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ ballot' = s
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, posted, atBreaker>>

CastVote(p) ==
    /\ ballot # NoOne
    /\ p \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, epoch, holder, posted, atBreaker>>

CommitBallot ==
    /\ ballot # NoOne
    /\ tally = Participants
    /\ holder' = ballot
    /\ posted' = posted \cup {[to |-> ballot, stamp |-> epoch]}
    /\ ballot' = NoOne
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, atBreaker>>

AbandonBallot ==
    /\ ballot # NoOne
    /\ ballot' = NoOne
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, posted, atBreaker>>

\* Only a notice stamped with the current epoch is a live grant.
TakeBreaker(n) ==
    /\ n \in posted
    /\ n.stamp = epoch
    /\ atBreaker' = atBreaker \cup {n.to}
    /\ posted' = posted \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, epoch, tally, holder>>

DropNotice(n) ==
    /\ n \in posted
    /\ n.stamp # epoch
    /\ posted' = posted \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, epoch, tally, holder, atBreaker>>

StandDown(s) ==
    /\ s \in atBreaker
    /\ atBreaker' = atBreaker \ {s}
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, epoch, tally, posted>>

\* An unused grant lapses once its notice is out of circulation, so the breaker is
\* never left ownerless while a live grant for it is still on the bus.
Lapse ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ holder \notin atBreaker
    /\ ~(\E n \in posted : n.to = holder /\ n.stamp = epoch)
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, epoch, tally, posted, atBreaker>>

\* The cold restart is safe only because it takes every circulating notice with
\* it; a notice surviving the epoch reset would read as live again.
ColdRestart ==
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = 0
    /\ posted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, tally, holder, atBreaker>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Substations : OpenBallot(s)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : CastVote(p)
    \/ CommitBallot
    \/ AbandonBallot
    \/ \E n \in Notices : TakeBreaker(n)
    \/ \E n \in Notices : DropNotice(n)
    \/ \E s \in Substations : StandDown(s)
    \/ Lapse
    \/ ColdRestart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BreakerExclusion ==
    \A s \in Substations : s \in atBreaker => holder = s

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Substations = {subQuarry, subDelta}
    Participants = {subQuarry, subDelta, ctlCentre}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoOne = noOne

INVARIANT BreakerExclusion
nl:
A power-grid load shedder has one islanding breaker that only a single substation may
operate at a time. The right to operate it is granted through a two-phase commit: the
control centre opens a ballot naming the substation that asked for it, every participant on
the interlock bus votes, and only a unanimous ballot is committed. Each ballot carries an
interlock epoch number, and committing a ballot records the named substation as the holder
and posts it a grant notice stamped with that epoch.

Grant notices travel the bus out of order and can sit around long after the ballot that
produced them. A substation therefore acts on a notice only when the stamp on it is the
interlock's current epoch; a notice carrying any other stamp is a leftover from a bygone
ballot and is thrown away unread.

The shedder behaves as follows. The control centre may open a ballot for a substation when
no ballot is open, the breaker has no holder, and the epoch budget is not spent; opening
advances the interlock epoch and clears the tally. Any participant that has not yet voted
on the open ballot may vote. The control centre commits the open ballot once every
participant has voted, recording the named substation as the holder and posting it a grant
notice stamped with the current epoch. The control centre may instead abandon the open
ballot, which posts nothing. A substation may act on a notice addressed to it whose stamp
is the current epoch, taking up the breaker and consuming the notice. A notice whose stamp
is not the current epoch is discarded. A substation at the breaker may stand down, which
leaves the breaker with no holder. A grant that its holder never took up may lapse once no
live notice for that holder is still in circulation, which also leaves the breaker with no
holder. When the epoch budget is spent the control centre may
cold-restart the interlock, discarding every notice still in circulation and returning the
epoch to zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every substation that is at the breaker is the substation the control
centre records as the breaker's holder, so two substations can never be operating it at
once.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, NumNodes, Capacity, PerNode, MaxGen, Step

\* The token goes to the neighbour or the node past it, so a stalled node can be
\* stepped over without waiting for it.
Onward(n, k) == ((n + k - 1) % NumNodes) + 1

VARIABLES load, gen, held, dead

vars == <<load, gen, held, dead>>

RECURSIVE Connected(_)
Connected(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN load[n] + Connected(S \ {n})

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Nodes -> 0..PerNode]
    /\ gen \in 1..MaxGen
    /\ held \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ dead \in SUBSET Nodes

Init ==
    /\ load = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ gen = 1
    /\ held = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ dead = {}

Live(n) == n \notin dead /\ held[n] = gen

\* Nobody alive is holding the generation that is current: the ring is stranded.
Stranded == \A n \in Nodes : held[n] = gen => n \in dead

Connect(n, d) ==
    /\ Live(n)
    /\ load[n] + d <= PerNode
    /\ Connected(Nodes) + d <= Capacity
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![n] = @ + d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, held, dead>>

Shed(n, d) ==
    /\ Live(n)
    /\ load[n] >= d
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![n] = @ - d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, held, dead>>

HandOn(n, k) ==
    /\ Live(n)
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![n] = 0, ![Onward(n, k)] = gen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, dead>>

Regenerate(m) ==
    /\ Stranded
    /\ m \notin dead
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = gen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, dead>>

Fail(n) ==
    /\ n \notin dead
    /\ Cardinality(dead) < Cardinality(Nodes) - 1
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, gen, held>>

ReForm(m) ==
    /\ gen = MaxGen
    /\ m \notin dead
    /\ gen' = 1
    /\ held' = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = m THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, dead>>

Reseating == \E m \in Nodes : Regenerate(m) \/ ReForm(m)

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, d \in 1..Step : Connect(n, d) \/ Shed(n, d)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, k \in 1..2 : HandOn(n, k)
    \/ Reseating
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Reseating)

WithinCapacity == Connected(Nodes) <= Capacity

TokenReturnsToRing == Stranded ~> ~Stranded

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {1, 2, 3}
    NumNodes = 3
    Capacity = 3
    PerNode = 2
    MaxGen = 3
    Step = 2

INVARIANT WithinCapacity
PROPERTY TokenReturnsToRing
nl:
A power-grid load shedder controls how much load each of its nodes may connect to a shared
feed. The feed has a fixed capacity that the connected load across all nodes must never
exceed, and each node has its own smaller per-node ceiling. The right to change connected
load travels the nodes as a token, and the token carries a generation number: a node may
only change load while the generation it is holding is the ring's current generation.

A node can fail silently, and it can fail while holding the token, which strands the ring.
The other nodes cannot tell a failed node from a slow one, so any surviving node may
regenerate the token when no live node is holding the current generation, which mints the
next generation for itself and leaves the stranded generation behind for good. When the
generation numbers run out the ring is re-formed from scratch: the numbering restarts and a
surviving node is seated with the first generation while every other node is left holding
nothing.

The shedder behaves as follows. A surviving node holding the current generation may connect
an increment of load, provided that doing so keeps it under its own ceiling and keeps the
total connected load across all nodes within the feed's capacity. A surviving node holding
the current generation may equally shed an increment of load it has connected. A surviving
node holding the current generation may hand the token onward to its neighbour or the node
past it, minting the next generation for that node and giving up its own. Any surviving node
may regenerate the token when no live node holds the current generation. Any node may fail
silently, so long as not every node has failed. When the generation budget is spent, a
surviving node may re-form the ring, restarting the numbering with itself seated.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total load connected across all nodes never exceeds the feed's
capacity.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the token is stranded, with no live node holding the ring's
current generation, some live node eventually holds it again.

---- MODULE W4Od11m0p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Operators, Jobs, MaxPriority, MaxVersion, NoStamp

Tables == [Jobs -> 0..MaxPriority]
Blank == [j \in Jobs |-> 0]

VARIABLES table, stamp, snapshot, snapStamp, outstanding

vars == <<table, stamp, snapshot, snapStamp, outstanding>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ table \in Tables
    /\ stamp \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ snapshot \in [Operators -> Tables]
    /\ snapStamp \in [Operators -> {NoStamp} \cup (0..MaxVersion)]
    /\ outstanding \in [Operators -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ table = Blank
    /\ stamp = 0
    /\ snapshot = [o \in Operators |-> Blank]
    /\ snapStamp = [o \in Operators |-> NoStamp]
    /\ outstanding = [o \in Operators |-> FALSE]

Fetch(o) ==
    /\ ~outstanding[o]
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![o] = table]
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![o] = stamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<table, stamp, outstanding>>

Submit(o) ==
    /\ ~outstanding[o]
    /\ snapStamp[o] # NoStamp
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![o] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<table, stamp, snapshot, snapStamp>>

\* The write-back replaces the whole table, so the stamp test is the only thing
\* keeping an overtaken snapshot from erasing what landed while it was in flight.
Accept(o, j, p) ==
    /\ outstanding[o]
    /\ snapStamp[o] = stamp
    /\ stamp < MaxVersion
    /\ table' = [snapshot[o] EXCEPT ![j] = p]
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![o] = [snapshot[o] EXCEPT ![j] = p]]
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![o] = stamp + 1]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![o] = FALSE]

\* An overtaken write-back is refused and its snapshot discarded; the operator
\* has to fetch afresh rather than resubmit what it already had.
Refuse(o) ==
    /\ outstanding[o]
    /\ (snapStamp[o] # stamp \/ stamp = MaxVersion)
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![o] = Blank]
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![o] = NoStamp]
    /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![o] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<table, stamp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Operators : Fetch(o)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : Submit(o)
    \/ \E o \in Operators, j \in Jobs, p \in 0..MaxPriority : Accept(o, j, p)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : Refuse(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A o \in Operators : snapStamp[o] = stamp => snapshot[o] = table

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Operators = {opFront, opBindery}
    Jobs = {jobFlyer, jobLedger}
    MaxPriority = 1
    MaxVersion = 2
    NoStamp = noStamp

INVARIANT CurrentStampMeansCurrentCopy
nl:
A print shop job spooler keeps one shared priority table listing a priority for every queued
job. Operators do not edit the table in place. An operator fetches a snapshot of the whole
table together with the spooler's version stamp, works out the change it wants, and submits
a write-back that replaces the entire table. Because the write-back replaces everything,
the spooler accepts it only while the stamp the operator fetched is still the spooler's
current stamp; otherwise the operator's snapshot has been overtaken and its write-back
would erase whatever landed in the meantime, so the submission is refused and the operator
must fetch again and retry.

Several operators may have write-backs outstanding at once, and the spooler works through
them in whatever order it reaches them rather than the order they were submitted. That is
how a write-back submitted first can be refused because one submitted later was applied
first.

The spooler behaves as follows. An operator with nothing outstanding may fetch the table,
recording the snapshot and the stamp it saw. An operator holding a stamped snapshot and
with nothing outstanding may submit its write-back. The spooler may accept an outstanding
write-back when the stamp it was built on is still current and the version budget is not
spent, replacing the table with the operator's snapshot carrying one job's priority changed,
advancing the stamp, and handing the operator back a snapshot of the new table stamped with
the new version. The spooler may refuse an outstanding write-back whose stamp is no longer
current, or any write-back at all once the version budget is spent, which throws away the
operator's snapshot and leaves it to fetch again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any operator whose recorded stamp is the spooler's current stamp is holding
an exact copy of the live table, so a write-back that the spooler will accept can never have
been built on a table that has already moved on.

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS LineA, LineB, Bays, ShiftLength, LeaseSpan, NoOne, NoBay

Stations == LineA \cup LineB

\* The two conveyor lines draw on one pool, so which line a station belongs to
\* decides whether the pool already owes that line a bay.
LineOf(s) == IF s \in LineA THEN LineA ELSE LineB

VARIABLES clock, lessee, deadline, busy

vars == <<clock, lessee, deadline, busy>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..ShiftLength
    /\ lessee \in [Bays -> {NoOne} \cup Stations]
    /\ deadline \in [Bays -> 0..ShiftLength]
    /\ busy \in [Stations -> {NoBay} \cup Bays]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ lessee = [b \in Bays |-> NoOne]
    /\ deadline = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ busy = [s \in Stations |-> NoBay]

UnderLiveLease(s) == lessee[busy[s]] = s /\ deadline[busy[s]] > clock

Grant(s, b) ==
    /\ busy[s] = NoBay
    /\ lessee[b] = NoOne
    /\ \A x \in LineOf(s) : \A c \in Bays : lessee[c] # x
    /\ clock + LeaseSpan <= ShiftLength
    /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![b] = s]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![b] = clock + LeaseSpan]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, busy>>

Start(s, b) ==
    /\ busy[s] = NoBay
    /\ lessee[b] = s
    /\ deadline[b] > clock
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lessee, deadline>>

Stop(s) ==
    /\ busy[s] # NoBay
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![s] = NoBay]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lessee, deadline>>

Renew(s, b) ==
    /\ lessee[b] = s
    /\ deadline[b] > clock
    /\ clock + LeaseSpan <= ShiftLength
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![b] = clock + LeaseSpan]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lessee, busy>>

\* A tick that reaches a deadline pulls the station out of the bay there and then.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < ShiftLength
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ busy' = [s \in Stations |->
                  IF busy[s] # NoBay /\ deadline[busy[s]] <= clock + 1
                  THEN NoBay ELSE busy[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, deadline>>

Reclaim(b) ==
    /\ lessee[b] # NoOne
    /\ deadline[b] <= clock
    /\ \A s \in Stations : busy[s] # b
    /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, deadline, busy>>

NewShift ==
    /\ clock = ShiftLength
    /\ \A b \in Bays : lessee[b] = NoOne
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ deadline' = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, busy>>

Reclaiming == \E b \in Bays : Reclaim(b)

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Stations, b \in Bays : Grant(s, b) \/ Start(s, b) \/ Renew(s, b)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Stop(s)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Reclaiming
    \/ NewShift

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick) /\ WF_vars(Reclaiming)

NoWorkWithoutLiveLease ==
    \A s \in Stations : busy[s] # NoBay => UnderLiveLease(s)

EveryLeasedBayReturns ==
    \A b \in Bays : (lessee[b] # NoOne) ~> (lessee[b] = NoOne)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    LineA = {stFoam, stRinse}
    LineB = {stWax}
    Bays = {bayNorth, baySouth}
    ShiftLength = 3
    LeaseSpan = 2
    NoOne = noOne
    NoBay = noBay

INVARIANT NoWorkWithoutLiveLease
PROPERTY EveryLeasedBayReturns
nl:
A car-wash site runs two independent conveyor lines that share one pool of wash bays. A
station takes a bay by holding a lease on it: the lease records the station as the bay's
lessee and carries a deadline on the site clock. A station may only work in a bay while it
is that bay's recorded lessee and the lease deadline is still ahead of the clock. To keep
the two lines from monopolising the pool, a line may hold at most one lease across all of
its stations at a time.

Leases expire on their own. When the site clock ticks past a lease deadline the station
working under it is pulled out of the bay immediately, and the expired lease is later
reclaimed so the bay returns to the pool. A shift lasts a bounded number of ticks; once the
clock has run out and every bay is back in the pool, a fresh shift starts with the clock
back at zero.

The site behaves as follows. A station with no bay in hand may be granted a lease on a free
bay, provided no station on its line already holds a lease and the lease deadline would fall
within the shift; the lease deadline is set a fixed span ahead of the clock. A station that
is the lessee of a bay whose deadline is still ahead may start working in that bay. A
station working in a bay may stop. A station that is a bay's lessee may renew the lease
while its deadline is still ahead, pushing the deadline a fixed span past the clock, so long
as that stays within the shift. The clock may tick, which pulls out of their bays every
station whose lease deadline has been reached. An expired lease on a bay nobody is working
in may be reclaimed, returning the bay to the pool. When the shift clock has run out and no
bay is leased, a fresh shift may begin with the clock back at zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every station working in a bay is that bay's recorded lessee and its lease
deadline is still ahead of the site clock, so no station ever works on a stale or borrowed
lease.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every leased bay is eventually returned to the pool.

---- MODULE W4Od17m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Intake, Arm, Belt, Chute, MinLimit, MaxLimit, MaxRetunes

Places == {Intake, Arm, Belt, Chute}

VARIABLES at, manifest, limit, retunes

vars == <<at, manifest, limit, retunes>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ at \in [Bags -> Places]
    /\ manifest \in [Places -> SUBSET Bags]
    /\ limit \in MinLimit..MaxLimit
    /\ retunes \in 0..MaxRetunes

Init ==
    /\ at = [b \in Bags |-> Intake]
    /\ manifest = [p \in Places |-> IF p = Intake THEN Bags ELSE {}]
    /\ limit = MinLimit
    /\ retunes = 0

\* Every move touches both views at once; that is the whole discipline.
Move(b, from, to) ==
    /\ at[b] = from
    /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![b] = to]
    /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![from] = @ \ {b}, ![to] = @ \cup {b}]

PickUp(b) ==
    /\ manifest[Arm] = {}
    /\ Move(b, Intake, Arm)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, retunes>>

\* Backpressure: the belt takes nothing more once it has reached its limit.
PlaceOnBelt(b) ==
    /\ Cardinality(manifest[Belt]) < limit
    /\ Move(b, Arm, Belt)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, retunes>>

PushBack(b) ==
    /\ Cardinality(manifest[Belt]) >= limit
    /\ Move(b, Arm, Intake)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, retunes>>

Deliver(b) ==
    /\ Move(b, Belt, Chute)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, retunes>>

Resort(b) ==
    /\ Move(b, Chute, Intake)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, retunes>>

\* The limit may be retuned below what the belt is already carrying; the belt
\* simply stops accepting until it has drained.
Retune(v) ==
    /\ retunes < MaxRetunes
    /\ v # limit
    /\ limit' = v
    /\ retunes' = retunes + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<at, manifest>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags : PickUp(b) \/ PlaceOnBelt(b) \/ PushBack(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Deliver(b) \/ Resort(b)
    \/ \E v \in MinLimit..MaxLimit : Retune(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BagsConserved ==
    \A p \in Places : manifest[p] = {b \in Bags : at[b] = p}

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Bags = {bagRed, bagBlue, bagGrey}
    Intake = intake
    Arm = arm
    Belt = belt
    Chute = chute
    MinLimit = 1
    MaxLimit = 2
    MaxRetunes = 2

INVARIANT BagsConserved
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags between four places: the intake floor, the router arm,
the belt, and the delivery chute. The router keeps two views of where everything is -- a
per-bag record of the place that bag is in, and a per-place manifest listing the bags that
place is holding -- and every move has to update both views together, because a bag dropped
from one manifest without being added to the other has been destroyed, and a bag added
without being removed has been conjured out of nothing.

The belt is a bounded work queue and its bound is set at runtime: the operator may retune
the belt limit up or down a bounded number of times per session. Backpressure is applied at
the arm: a bag on the arm is placed on the belt only while the belt is holding fewer bags
than the current limit, and otherwise the arm returns it to the intake floor. Retuning the
limit downwards while the belt is already fuller than the new limit is allowed; the belt is
simply not given anything more until it has drained below the limit again.

The router behaves as follows. A bag on the intake floor may be picked up onto the arm while
the arm is empty. A bag on the arm may be placed on the belt while the belt holds fewer bags
than the current limit. A bag on the arm may instead be returned to the intake floor when
the belt is at or above the current limit. A bag on the belt may be delivered to the chute.
A bag in the chute may be sent back to the intake floor for re-sorting. The operator may
retune the belt limit to any value in the router's permitted range, so long as the session's
allowance of retunes is not spent.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every place's manifest lists exactly the bags whose own record says they
are in that place, so no bag is ever duplicated across two places or lost between them.

---- MODULE W4Od19m4p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branches, Reservations, Copies, ListLimit, NoCopy, NoRes

VARIABLES waiting, picked, given, heldFor

vars == <<waiting, picked, given, heldFor>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ waiting \in SUBSET Reservations
    /\ picked \in [Branches -> SUBSET Reservations]
    /\ given \in [Reservations -> {NoCopy} \cup Copies]
    /\ heldFor \in [Copies -> {NoRes} \cup Reservations]

Init ==
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ picked = [b \in Branches |-> {}]
    /\ given = [r \in Reservations |-> NoCopy]
    /\ heldFor = [c \in Copies |-> NoRes]

OnSomeList(r) == \E b \in Branches : r \in picked[b]

Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin waiting
    /\ ~OnSomeList(r)
    /\ given[r] = NoCopy
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<picked, given, heldFor>>

\* Backpressure: a branch at its limit takes nothing more onto its list.
Take(b, r) ==
    /\ r \in waiting
    /\ Cardinality(picked[b]) < ListLimit
    /\ picked' = [picked EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {r}]
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, heldFor>>

\* The copy leaves the shared pool for good; both records are written together.
Issue(b, r, c) ==
    /\ r \in picked[b]
    /\ heldFor[c] = NoRes
    /\ given[r] = NoCopy
    /\ given' = [given EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ heldFor' = [heldFor EXCEPT ![c] = r]
    /\ picked' = [picked EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED waiting

Drop(b, r) ==
    /\ r \in picked[b]
    /\ picked' = [picked EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {r}]
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, heldFor>>

Clear(r) ==
    \/ \E b \in Branches, c \in Copies : Issue(b, r, c)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : Drop(b, r)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reservations : Submit(r)
    \/ \E b \in Branches, r \in Reservations : Take(b, r)
    \/ \E r \in Reservations : Clear(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Reservations : WF_vars(Clear(r))

NoSecondIssue ==
    \A c \in Copies : heldFor[c] # NoRes => given[heldFor[c]] = c

EveryPickedReservationLeavesTheList ==
    \A r \in Reservations : OnSomeList(r) ~> ~OnSomeList(r)

====
nl:
A library reservation system runs two branches that work independently but draw physical
copies from one shared pool. A reservation waits in the system until a branch takes it onto
its pick list. Each pick list is a bounded work queue: a branch will not take on a new
reservation while its list is already at the branch's limit, which is the backpressure that
stops either branch from hoarding the queue.

Issuing a copy against a reservation is irreversible: the copy leaves the pool for good,
recorded as held against that reservation, and the reservation records the copy it received.
The two records are the system's only defence against handing a second copy to a reservation
that already has one, since a reservation quietly reissued would leave its first copy
recorded against it while the reservation itself pointed elsewhere.

The system behaves as follows. A reservation that is neither waiting, on a pick list, nor
already filled may be submitted, which puts it in the waiting set. A branch whose pick list
is below its limit may take a waiting reservation onto its list. A branch may issue a free
copy from the shared pool against a reservation on its list, which records the copy against
the reservation and the reservation against the copy and takes the reservation off the list.
A branch may instead drop a reservation from its list, returning it to the waiting set.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every copy recorded as held against a reservation is the very copy that
reservation records having received, so no reservation is ever filled a second time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every reservation that reaches a branch's pick list eventually leaves it.

---- MODULE W4Od0m4p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Theatres, MaxCases, MaxTotal, MaxAdd, QueueLimit, MaxOverrides

\* An amendment carries the running total it was worked out against; that stamp
\* is the only thing that can tell it apart from one built on a live total.
Amendments == [theatre : Theatres, adds : 1..MaxAdd, base : 0..MaxTotal]

VARIABLES running, cases, queue, overrides

vars == <<running, cases, queue, overrides>>

RECURSIVE Booked(_)
Booked(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET t == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN cases[t] + Booked(S \ {t})

TypeOK ==
    /\ running \in 0..MaxTotal
    /\ cases \in [Theatres -> 0..MaxCases]
    /\ queue \in SUBSET Amendments
    /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ running = 0
    /\ cases = [t \in Theatres |-> 0]
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ overrides = 0

Raise(a) ==
    /\ a \notin queue
    /\ a.base = running
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueLimit
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, cases, overrides>>

\* The consultant's override buys a place past the backpressure, nothing more:
\* the amendment still has to survive validation like any other.
Push(a) ==
    /\ a \notin queue
    /\ a.base = running
    /\ Cardinality(queue) >= QueueLimit
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {a}
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, cases>>

Fits(a) ==
    /\ a.base = running
    /\ running + a.adds <= MaxTotal
    /\ cases[a.theatre] + a.adds <= MaxCases

Apply(a) ==
    /\ a \in queue
    /\ Fits(a)
    /\ cases' = [cases EXCEPT ![a.theatre] = @ + a.adds]
    /\ running' = a.base + a.adds
    /\ queue' = queue \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED overrides

Drop(a) ==
    /\ a \in queue
    /\ ~Fits(a)
    /\ queue' = queue \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, cases, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Amendments : Raise(a) \/ Push(a)
    \/ \E a \in Amendments : Apply(a) \/ Drop(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TotalMatchesTheatres == running = Booked(Theatres)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Theatres = {thrOrtho, thrCardiac}
    MaxCases = 2
    MaxTotal = 3
    MaxAdd = 1
    QueueLimit = 1
    MaxOverrides = 1

INVARIANT TotalMatchesTheatres
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps a shared record of theatre workload: a per-theatre
list count and a running total across all theatres. Changes arrive as amendments held in a
bounded work queue. Each amendment names a theatre, the number of cases it adds, and the
running total the amendment was worked out against. Applying an amendment writes the new
running total absolutely, as the amendment's own base plus its cases, rather than nudging
whatever total happens to be there. That is why an amendment must be validated against the
live total before it is applied: one applied against a base that has since moved would write
back a total that never accounted for whatever landed in between.

The work queue applies backpressure: no further amendment is accepted once the queue is at
its limit. The duty consultant holds a privileged override and may push an amendment past a
full queue, a bounded number of times per session.

The scheduler behaves as follows. An amendment naming a theatre and a number of cases may be
raised while the queue is below its limit, stamped with the running total as it stands. The
duty consultant may instead push such an amendment onto a queue that is already at its
limit, spending one of the session's overrides. A queued amendment may be applied when the
total it was stamped against is still the live total and the change keeps both that
theatre's count and the running total within their ceilings, which raises the theatre's count
and writes the total as the amendment's base plus its cases. A queued amendment that fails
any of those tests is discarded unapplied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The running total always equals the sum of the per-theatre counts, so no
theatre's amendment is ever silently dropped out of the shared total.

---- MODULE W4Od16m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, MaxTerm, MaxLog

\* A request carries the term its author believed was in force; a takeover since
\* then is exactly what makes the stamp worthless.
Requests == [who : Stations, stamp : 1..MaxTerm]

VARIABLES log, told, leader, term, outstanding

vars == <<log, told, leader, term, outstanding>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ log \in Seq(Stations)
    /\ Len(log) <= MaxLog
    /\ told \in [Stations -> 0..MaxLog]
    /\ leader \in Stations
    /\ term \in 1..MaxTerm
    /\ outstanding \in SUBSET Requests

Init ==
    /\ log = << >>
    /\ told = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ leader \in Stations
    /\ term = 1
    /\ outstanding = {}

Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin outstanding
    /\ r.stamp = term
    /\ outstanding' = outstanding \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, told, leader, term>>

\* The log only ever grows at the end, and the author is told where its entry sits.
Write(r) ==
    /\ r \in outstanding
    /\ r.stamp = term
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ log' = Append(log, r.who)
    /\ told' = [told EXCEPT ![r.who] = Len(log) + 1]
    /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Refuse(r) ==
    /\ r \in outstanding
    /\ r.stamp # term
    /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, told, leader, term>>

DropFull(r) ==
    /\ r \in outstanding
    /\ r.stamp = term
    /\ Len(log) = MaxLog
    /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, told, leader, term>>

TakeOver(s) ==
    /\ s # leader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = s
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<log, told, outstanding>>

Resolve(r) == Write(r) \/ Refuse(r) \/ DropFull(r)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Submit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Resolve(r)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : TakeOver(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Requests : WF_vars(Resolve(r))

ConfirmedEntriesStand ==
    \A s \in Stations :
        told[s] # 0 => (told[s] <= Len(log) /\ log[told[s]] = s)

EveryRequestResolves ==
    \A r \in Requests : (r \in outstanding) ~> (r \notin outstanding)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Stations = {stnBench, stnWindow}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxLog = 2

INVARIANT ConfirmedEntriesStand
PROPERTY EveryRequestResolves
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser keeps its shared dispensing record as an append-only log.
One dispensing station acts as leader and is the only station that may write to the log; if
it is thought to have gone down another station takes over, and each takeover raises the
record's term number.

Stations do not write directly. A station submits an append request stamped with the term it
believes is in force, and requests reach the leader out of order and can be arbitrarily
delayed. A request stamped with a term that is no longer in force is refused rather than
written, because the station that raised it was working from a picture of the record that a
takeover has since replaced. When a request is written the log grows by one entry and the
station is told the index its entry landed at; that index and that entry are what the station
will rely on from then on. The log has a bounded length, and once it is full any request
still outstanding is dropped unwritten.

The dispenser behaves as follows. A station may submit an append request stamped with the
record's term as the station understands it. The leader may write an outstanding request
whose stamp is the term now in force while the log still has room, appending the requesting
station's entry and telling that station the index it landed at. An outstanding request whose
stamp is not the term now in force is refused. An outstanding request is dropped once the log
is full. Any station other than the current leader may take over, which raises the term.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a station has been told its entry landed at an index, the log is
still at least that long and that index still holds that station's entry, so no confirmed
write is ever overwritten or lost.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every append request that is submitted is eventually resolved and stops
being outstanding.

---- MODULE W4Od19m6p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Desks, MaxLease, SessionLength, Span

\* A grant names a desk and the lease number it carries; grants overtake each
\* other in transit, so the number is the only ordering a desk can trust.
Grants == [to : Desks, num : 1..MaxLease]

VARIABLES clock, issued, deadline, holds, driving, circulating

vars == <<clock, issued, deadline, holds, driving, circulating>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..SessionLength
    /\ issued \in 0..MaxLease
    /\ deadline \in 0..SessionLength
    /\ holds \in [Desks -> 0..MaxLease]
    /\ driving \in SUBSET Desks
    /\ circulating \in SUBSET Grants

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ issued = 0
    /\ deadline = 0
    /\ holds = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ driving = {}
    /\ circulating = {}

IssueLease(d) ==
    /\ deadline <= clock
    /\ issued < MaxLease
    /\ clock + Span <= SessionLength
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ deadline' = clock + Span
    /\ circulating' = circulating \cup {[to |-> d, num |-> issued + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holds, driving>>

Adopt(g) ==
    /\ g \in circulating
    /\ g.num > holds[g.to]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![g.to] = g.num]
    /\ circulating' = circulating \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, issued, deadline, driving>>

Straggler(g) ==
    /\ g \in circulating
    /\ g.num <= holds[g.to]
    /\ circulating' = circulating \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, issued, deadline, holds, driving>>

Take(d) ==
    /\ d \notin driving
    /\ holds[d] = issued
    /\ clock < deadline
    /\ driving' = driving \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, issued, deadline, holds, circulating>>

LetGo(d) ==
    /\ d \in driving
    /\ driving' = driving \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, issued, deadline, holds, circulating>>

Renew(d) ==
    /\ d \in driving
    /\ clock + Span <= SessionLength
    /\ deadline' = clock + Span
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, issued, holds, driving, circulating>>

\* Reaching the deadline takes whoever is driving straight off the robot.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < SessionLength
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ driving' = IF deadline > clock + 1 THEN driving ELSE {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, deadline, holds, circulating>>

NewSession ==
    /\ clock = SessionLength
    /\ driving = {}
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ issued' = 0
    /\ deadline' = 0
    /\ holds' = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ circulating' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED driving

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks : IssueLease(d) \/ Take(d) \/ LetGo(d) \/ Renew(d)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : Adopt(g) \/ Straggler(g)
    \/ Tick
    \/ NewSession

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RobotExclusion ==
    \A d \in Desks : d \in driving => (holds[d] = issued /\ clock < deadline)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Desks = {dskLending, dskArchive}
    MaxLease = 2
    SessionLength = 3
    Span = 2

INVARIANT RobotExclusion
nl:
A library reservation system has one stack-retrieval robot that only a single branch desk
may drive at a time. The right to drive it is a lease: the lease server issues leases with
strictly rising lease numbers and each lease carries a deadline on the session clock. Only
the desk holding the lease number that the server most recently issued, and only while the
deadline is still ahead of the clock, may drive the robot. The server will not issue a fresh
lease until the standing deadline has been reached.

Lease grants reach the desks out of order and can be arbitrarily delayed. A desk therefore
adopts an arriving grant only when its lease number is higher than the one the desk is
already holding; a grant carrying a number the desk has already passed is a straggler and is
thrown away. When the clock reaches the standing deadline, any desk driving the robot is
taken off it immediately.

The system behaves as follows. The server may issue the next lease number to a desk once the
standing deadline has been reached, provided the lease budget is not spent and the new
deadline would fall inside the session, and it puts a grant for that desk into circulation.
A circulating grant whose number is higher than what its desk holds is adopted by that desk.
A circulating grant whose number is not higher is discarded. A desk holding the most recently
issued lease number, with the deadline still ahead of the clock, may take the robot. A desk
driving the robot may let it go. A desk driving the robot may renew, pushing the deadline a
fixed span past the clock so long as that stays inside the session. The clock may tick, which
takes off the robot any desk whose deadline has been reached. When the session clock has run
out and nobody is driving, a fresh session may begin: the clock, the lease numbering, every
desk's held number, and all grants in circulation are reset.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every desk driving the robot is holding the most recently issued lease
number and the standing deadline is still ahead of the clock, so two desks can never be
driving it at once.

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branches, Copies, Shelf, Transit, Loaned, Quorum, MaxProposal, NoProposal

Pools == {Shelf, Transit, Loaned}
Moves == [copy : Copies, to : Pools]
Ballots == [voter : Branches, num : 1..MaxProposal]

VARIABLES pools, standing, number, cast

vars == <<pools, standing, number, cast>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pools \in [Pools -> SUBSET Copies]
    /\ standing \in {NoProposal} \cup Moves
    /\ number \in 0..MaxProposal
    /\ cast \in SUBSET Ballots

Init ==
    /\ pools = [p \in Pools |-> IF p = Shelf THEN Copies ELSE {}]
    /\ standing = NoProposal
    /\ number = 0
    /\ cast = {}

Where(c) == CHOOSE p \in Pools : c \in pools[p]

\* Only ballots carrying the standing number count; the late ones are noise.
Backing == Cardinality({b \in cast : b.num = number})

Propose(m) ==
    /\ standing = NoProposal
    /\ number < MaxProposal
    /\ m.to # Where(m.copy)
    /\ standing' = m
    /\ number' = number + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pools, cast>>

CastBallot(b) ==
    /\ b \notin cast
    /\ b.num <= number
    /\ cast' = cast \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pools, standing, number>>

\* Carrying the move takes the copy out of one pool and puts it in another in the
\* same step; there is no moment where it sits in both or neither.
Carry ==
    /\ standing # NoProposal
    /\ Backing >= Quorum
    /\ pools' = [pools EXCEPT ![Where(standing.copy)] = @ \ {standing.copy},
                              ![standing.to] = @ \cup {standing.copy}]
    /\ standing' = NoProposal
    /\ UNCHANGED <<number, cast>>

Abandon ==
    /\ standing # NoProposal
    /\ standing' = NoProposal
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pools, number, cast>>

Sweep(b) ==
    /\ b \in cast
    /\ b.num < number
    /\ cast' = cast \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pools, standing, number>>

Renumber ==
    /\ number = MaxProposal
    /\ standing = NoProposal
    /\ number' = 0
    /\ cast' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pools, standing>>

Settling == Carry \/ Abandon

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Moves : Propose(m)
    \/ \E b \in Ballots : CastBallot(b) \/ Sweep(b)
    \/ Settling
    \/ Renumber

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Branches = {brnHill, brnQuay, brnPark}
    Copies = {cpyAtlas, cpyOdes}
    Shelf = shelf
    Transit = transit
    Loaned = loaned
    Quorum = 2
    MaxProposal = 2
    NoProposal = noProposal

INVARIANT CopiesConserved
PROPERTY EveryProposalSettles
nl:
A library reservation system tracks where every physical copy sits. A copy is either on the
shelf, in transit between sites, or out on loan, and the system keeps each of those three
pools as a list of the copies it holds. Copies are neither manufactured nor destroyed by the
system, so a copy taken out of one pool must arrive in another and must never turn up in two
pools at once.

Moving a copy is not something any one desk decides. A move is proposed, given a proposal
number, and then voted on by the branches; only once a quorum of ballots has been cast for
the proposal number now standing may the move be carried out. Ballots arrive out of order and
late: a branch may cast a ballot carrying any proposal number the system has already reached,
so ballots for proposals long since settled keep turning up. Only ballots carrying the
standing proposal's number count towards its quorum, and stale ballots may be swept away.

The system behaves as follows. A move may be proposed when no proposal is standing and the
proposal budget is not spent, naming a copy and a destination pool that is not the pool the
copy is currently in; proposing takes the next proposal number. A branch may cast a ballot
carrying any proposal number the system has reached, if it has not already cast that ballot.
The standing proposal may be carried out once a quorum of ballots carrying its number has
been cast, which takes the copy out of the pool holding it and puts it in the destination
pool. The standing proposal may instead be abandoned at any time. A ballot carrying a
proposal number below the one now standing may be swept away. When the proposal budget is
spent and no proposal is standing, the system may start a fresh round of numbering, clearing
every ballot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every copy appears in exactly one of the three pools, so no copy is ever
duplicated across pools or lost between them.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal that comes to stand is eventually settled, either carried
out or abandoned.
